actionable_comment_findings.classification: Retained unsupported general performance claim; documentation only
actionable_comment_findings.mismatch: Intro claims compute kernels run about ten times faster than every CPU core without identifying measured hardware, CPU implementation, workload, conditions or a current benchmark source. The existing fixture only emits its own GPU elapsed times. No cross-provider runtime or comparative performance validation was supplied, so this prose exceeds documented validation limits. This is not a claim that kernels are slower.
actionable_comment_findings.evidence: Complete owning file and existing fixture read; actual fabelgeist-hair GPU intro1-88 describes independent GPU work but supplies no comparative benchmark. Focused owning hair-source search located only this comparison. Source inspection cannot establish the multiplier.
actionable_comment_findings.connected_repair: Remove the multiplier/general comparison and retain the architectural reason that independent strand sweeps run as compute kernels. Alternatively cite an already existing reproducible bounded observation with exact hardware/workload; no new benchmark/test is requested or authorized by this review.
actionable_comment_findings.acceptance: The nine-file handoff no longer presents an unqualified GPU/CPU speed ratio; all runtime/shader/fixture inputs/oracles stay unchanged and successor comments re-reviewed.

confirmed_contracts.evidence: Factory admits fixed2048 base and halves to1. Each positive side uses four-byte texels; row stride max(side,64) yields256-byte alignment because every side is power-of-two. Level offsets/complete byte extent include final row padding, and full extent checked for usize/isize/native u32 words before publication. Private layout/levels prevent arbitrary side/offset construction; readonly ports preserve same chain layout. No arbitrary texture-recipe/device-limit/geometry guarantee inferred.

ScalpMap mapped_side is square root of estimated mapped area in Metres; texel divides by admitted positive texture side. Physical shadow span and blur radius round using existing metre-to-texel ratio then clamp to at least one texel. ShadowBlockAxisCount ceil(side/block_span) is positive and no larger than2048, separate from texels. Shadow array elements are blocks squared while topmost/bare/finish use visible texel populations. WGSL uses matching block index and guarded64-lane folded item index. No new finite/clamp/tuning policy or geometry rewrite.

confirmed_contracts.area: Native chain provenance and host read
confirmed_contracts.evidence: Each chain privately owns Buffer, Arc layout and cloned actual creating Device. Factory allocates full padded extent, native operations finish/submit before successful bake return. Host read explicitly rejects different actual Device before prefix/copy/map work, reads exact admitted prefix and strips each padded row to visibleRGBA. Buffer read retains creating Device/pairedQueue and external mapping obligations, actual causes, native wait/browser yield and no later-health promise. Cardinality does not certify arbitrary source contents or native provider acceptance.

ScalpUploads retains actual chain+image handle until prepared. Image descriptor has admitted base side/mip count and Rgba8Unorm; copied mips use exact layout byte offset/row pitch and visible extent. Texture data is not brought through CPU in this preview upload path. Direct Bevy encoder/queue submit has configured error handling and no synchronous operation verdict, as explicitly documented. Pending is removed after recording, so no rollback/retry/completion guarantee is made. Host read explicit Device guard is a separate stronger boundary, not falsely claimed for Bevy queue copies.

HairGpu.finish async Result delegates canonical submitted_work_done; native explicit marker index and actual causes, browser callback/rejection caveat and earlier-producing-result requirement retained. Stage now holds two ScalpTextureChain values and completion calls already retain their fallible adapters. Existing settle/capture frame budgets are authored fixture scheduling, not proof that arbitrary file writes or all later GPU work complete. No native/browser/runtime/performance verdict inferred.
